before:
name: recstl_playground
description: >
  One-stop RectSL playground. Drops in a Window + Renderer, a hackable #rectsl
  snippet, and transport controls (play / loop / speed / time-scrub) in the
  playground box's output area. Edit the `rectsl` string and re-run to change it
  live; scrub the "time" slider to freeze on a frame, or check "play" to loop it.
operations:
  # 1. renderer box — owns the on-screen Window + Renderer and pumps the loop.
  - create:
      box: recstl_renderer
      name: window + renderer
      frame: { x: 40.0, y: 40.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.util.Options
          
          prop<Window>(window)
          prop<Renderer>(renderer)
          
          Options.enableHDR = false
          
          once.renderer {
              window = Window("RectSL playground")
              Renderer(window)
          }
          
          println("recstl renderer ready")
          start(renderer::run)
  # 2. playground box — compiles the snippet, draws it live, and publishes the
  #    transport controls. This is the box you hack on.
  - create:
      box: recstl_playground
      name: recstl
      frame: { x: 300.0, y: 140.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          RectSL playground.

          Edit the `rectsl` program below and re-run this box to change it live.
          The transport controls in this box's output area drive the clock:
            play  — advance time every frame and loop the animation
            loop  — wrap at the end (off = run once and hold on the last frame)
            speed — playback rate multiplier
            time  — scrub to a frame (while paused); moving it freezes the clock there

          See the "RectSL examples" docs page / rectsl_cheatsheet.md for the language.
          */
          import afield.lang.rectsl.RECT_ANIMATION_VERTEX_SHADER
          import afield.lang.rectsl.RectAnimationOracle
          import afield.lang.rectsl.rectMaterialShaderCode
          import afield.lang.rectsl.writeFrameToMesh

          val rectsl =
              """
          #rectsl
          ->wall 16 9 meters
          ->duration 6
          ->fps 30

          material spectrum '(
            uv 3.0 * time 0.5 * + fbm palette
          )

          "bar" rect
            0 0 ->xy
            0.9 1 ->wh
            '( 0 0.6  0.75 6.5  1.5 0.6 ) 1.5 loop-time ->h
            0xffffff solid ->fill
            spectrum ->material
          ;

          16 '(
            "bar" ->select clone
              i 7.5 - 1.2 * 0 ->xy
              i 0.14 * ->delay-all-time
          ) repeat
          """

          val program = RectAnimationOracle.compile(rectsl).program!!
          val shader = rectMaterialShaderCode(program)

          /*
          Seed this box's shader-source properties before `moduleHere {}` runs.
          moduleHere builds its module from the box's `vertex`/`fragment` properties
          (not from assignments in the lambda); `once.vertex`/`once.fragment` set them
          once. Fragments separated by `//%-` run one at a time, each expanded only after the
          previous one ran, so this fragment executes first and the moduleHere fragment then
          prepares its shaders from what was set here.
          */
          once.vertex { RECT_ANIMATION_VERTEX_SHADER }
          once.fragment { shader.exampleFragmentShader!! }

          //%-

          val module = moduleHere {
              blend = true
              depthTest = false
              primitiveType = triangles
          }
          val m = Mesh()
          module += "scene" to m
          renderer += "rectsl" to module

          val ww = program.wall.width.toFloat()
          val wh = program.wall.height.toFloat()
          m.push["worldToClip"] = afield.math.linalg.Matrix4f().ortho(-ww / 2f, ww / 2f, -wh / 2f, wh / 2f, -1f, 1f)
          m.push["wallWidth"] = ww
          m.push["wallHeight"] = wh

          // --- transport state, driven by the controls below ---
          val duration = program.duration.toDouble()
          var playing = true
          var looping = true
          var speed = 1.0
          var t = 0.0

          controlGroup("transport") {
              checkbox("play", initialValue = playing) { playing = it }
              checkbox("loop", initialValue = looping) { looping = it }
              slider("speed", min = 0.0, max = 3.0, step = 0.05, initialValue = speed) { speed = it }
              slider("time", min = 0.0, max = duration, step = 0.01, initialValue = 0.0) {
                  // Scrubbing the timeline while paused sets the clock; while playing it is ignored.
                  if (!playing) t = it
              }
          }

          loop {
              if (playing) {
                  t += (1.0 / 60.0) * speed
                  if (t > duration) t = if (looping) t - duration else duration
              }
              val sampleTime = if (looping) t % duration else t.coerceIn(0.0, duration)
              m.push["time"] = t.toFloat()
              program.writeFrameToMesh(sampleTime, m)
              true
          }
  # 3. wire the playground under the renderer so it inherits Window/Renderer.
  - connect: { parent: recstl_renderer, child: recstl_playground }
  # 4. launch the renderer first (it owns the loop), then the playground.
  - launch: { box: recstl_renderer, property: code, strand: renderer }
  - await: { wait: pending }
  - launch: { box: recstl_playground, property: code }
  - await: { wait: pending }

before:
name: rectsl_dataviz
description: >
  Loadable demo of the RectSL data-visualization family. Drops in a Window +
  Renderer and one #rectsl program that draws a live figure: a viridis colour-bar
  legend across the top (built with `array` + the `colormap` word) and a bar chart
  underneath, its heights and colours both bound to a numeric list via `data`,
  `normalize`, and `bars`, animated in with a staggered eased `->alpha`. Edit the
  `rectsl` string and re-run the box to change it live. Replay this file into a
  fresh Field with the agent backdoor (field_run_transcript) to see the whole
  family on screen with no other setup.

  # 1. renderer box — owns the on-screen Window + Renderer and pumps the loop.

      box: dataviz_renderer

      box: dataviz_figure
      name: rectsl dataviz
      frame: { x: 300.0, y: 140.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*

          ->wall 20 10 meters

          ->fps 30

          # colour legend across the top: 40 swatches sweeping viridis
          "leg" rect  0.5 0.8 ->wh
            40 '( fc 9.6 *  4.3 ->offset  "viridis" f colormap solid ->fill ) array

          # bar chart from data, viridis by value, staggered grow-in
          '( 4 7 2 9 5 8 3 6 1 6 5 9 4 7 3 8 ) data  normalize  "viridis" bars

              primitiveType = triangles
          }
          val m = Mesh()
          module += "scene" to m
          renderer += "rectsl-dataviz" to module

          val ww = program.wall.width.toFloat()
          val wh = program.wall.height.toFloat()
          m.push["worldToClip"] = afield.math.linalg.Matrix4f().ortho(-ww / 2f, ww / 2f, -wh / 2f, wh / 2f, -1f, 1f)
          m.push["wallWidth"] = ww
          m.push["wallHeight"] = wh

          val duration = program.duration.toDouble()
          var t = 0.0
          loop {
              m.push["time"] = t.toFloat()
              program.writeFrameToMesh(t % duration, m)
              t += 1.0 / 60.0
              true
          }

before:
name: rectsl_musicality
description: >
  Loadable demo of RectSL's musical layer — the Tidal-inspired pattern language used
  as scene structure. Drops in a Window + Renderer and one #rectsl program running on
  a musical clock (`->tempo 120`, `->duration-cycles`): a kick built with `pat` (one
  live copy per pattern event, each authored in its own local time), a five-against-
  sixteen hat ring from `array` + `->euclid` turned by `saw` read as a rotation track,
  a `->every 4` bar-line accent, and the same mini-notation string read as a ruler by
  `strip`. Edit the `rectsl` string and re-run the box to change the groove live —
  try `"bd*4"` -> `"bd(3,8)"`, or add `mini 4 iter` before the quote. Replay this file
  into a fresh Field with the agent backdoor (field_run_transcript) to see it on
  screen with no other setup.
operations:
  # 1. renderer box — owns the on-screen Window + Renderer and pumps the loop.
  - create:
      box: music_renderer
      name: window + renderer
      frame: { x: 40.0, y: 40.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.util.Options
          
          prop<Window>(window)
          prop<Renderer>(renderer)
          
          Options.enableHDR = false
          
          once.renderer {
              window = Window("RectSL — musicality")
              Renderer(window)
          }
          
          println("musicality renderer ready")
          start(renderer::run)
  # 2. groove box — compiles the snippet and draws it live. This is the box you hack on.
  - create:
      box: music_groove
      name: rectsl musicality
      frame: { x: 300.0, y: 140.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          RectSL's musical layer: the pattern language as scene structure.

          Two facts do all the work. A RectSL track is `sample(t)` and a pattern is
          `events(arc)` — both pure functions of time — so (1) a pattern IS a track,
          which is why `saw ->rotate` needs no conversion word, and (2) a pattern
          event carries an onset and a real duration, which is exactly what
          `->live birth life` wants, so an event IS a life window. `pat` is `array`
          indexed by rhythm instead of by ordinal.

          Nothing below is written in seconds. Edit `rectsl` and re-run to change the
          groove live. See rectsl_cheatsheet.md ("Musicality") / rectsl_examples.md.
          */
          import afield.lang.rectsl.RECT_ANIMATION_VERTEX_SHADER
          import afield.lang.rectsl.RectAnimationOracle
          import afield.lang.rectsl.rectMaterialShaderCode
          import afield.lang.rectsl.writeFrameToMesh

          val rectsl =
              """
          #rectsl
          ->wall 16 9 abstract
          ->tempo 120
          ->beats-per-cycle 4
          ->duration-cycles 4
          ->fps 30
          ->background 0x0a0a12

          # The accent: a full-wall flash, behind everything, on every fourth bar only.
          # This is the thing a loop cannot do and a groove must — `->every` keeps both
          # versions of every track and chooses between them per sample.
          "accent" rect
            16 9 ->wh
            0 0 ->xy
            0xffffff solid ->fill
            0 ->alpha
            ->back
            selected 4 '( 0.14 ->alpha ) ->every
          ;

          # The ring: sixteen slots in space, five of them sounding, the whole figure
          # turning once a bar because `saw` is a pattern read as a rotation track.
          "ring" group
            "hat" rect
              0.26 1.0 ->wh
              0x7cf5d0 solid ->fill
              16 '( f0 tau * ->rot  f0 tau * 3.2 ->polar ) array
              5 16 0 ->euclid
            ;
          end
          "ring" ->select
            saw tau * ->rotate
          ;

          # The kick: one copy per event, each ->live for exactly its own quarter and
          # authored in ITS OWN local time — so sixteen strikes, not a synchronised
          # chorus. `step` places each one across the wall, restarting at every bar line.
          "kick" rect
            1.3 ->square
            0xff5a3c solid ->fill
            "bd*4" '(
                step 1.5 - 4.2 *  ->x
                '( 0=5.5  0.34=0 ) ease-out ->y
                '( 0=0  0.10=1  0.5=0 ) linear ->alpha
            ) pat
          ;

          # The score: the same kind of string, read as a ruler instead of as a rhythm.
          # `pat` spends the subdivision on WHEN, `strip` spends it on WHERE.
          "tick" rect
            0.34 ->square
            0x3c8cff solid ->fill
            "bd [sd sd] hh*4" '( -3.9 ->y  0.55 ->alpha ) strip
          ;
          """

          val program = RectAnimationOracle.compile(rectsl).program!!
          val shader = rectMaterialShaderCode(program)

          /*
          Seed this box's shader-source properties before `moduleHere {}` runs; the
          `//%-` fragment break makes this fragment execute first (see the playground
          transcript for the why).
          */
          once.vertex { RECT_ANIMATION_VERTEX_SHADER }
          once.fragment { shader.exampleFragmentShader!! }

          //%-

          val module = moduleHere {
              blend = true
              depthTest = false
              primitiveType = triangles
          }
          val m = Mesh()
          module += "scene" to m
          renderer += "rectsl-musicality" to module

          val ww = program.wall.width.toFloat()
          val wh = program.wall.height.toFloat()
          m.push["worldToClip"] = afield.math.linalg.Matrix4f().ortho(-ww / 2f, ww / 2f, -wh / 2f, wh / 2f, -1f, 1f)
          m.push["wallWidth"] = ww
          m.push["wallHeight"] = wh

          val duration = program.duration.toDouble()
          var t = 0.0
          loop {
              m.push["time"] = t.toFloat()
              program.writeFrameToMesh(t % duration, m)
              t += 1.0 / 60.0
              true
          }
  # 3. wire the groove under the renderer so it inherits Window/Renderer.
  - connect: { parent: music_renderer, child: music_groove }
  # 4. launch the renderer first (it owns the loop), then the groove.
  - launch: { box: music_renderer, property: code, strand: renderer }
  - await: { wait: pending }
  - launch: { box: music_groove, property: code }
  - await: { wait: pending }

  sixteen hat ring from `array` + `->euclid` turned by `saw` read as a rotation track,
  a `->every 4` bar-line accent, and the same mini-notation string read as a ruler by
  `strip`. Edit the `rectsl` string and re-run the box to change the groove live —
  try `"bd*4"` -> `"bd(3,8)"`, or add `mini 4 iter` before the quote. Replay this file
  into a fresh Field with the agent backdoor (field_run_transcript) to see it on
  screen with no other setup.
operations:
  # 1. renderer box — owns the on-screen Window + Renderer and pumps the loop.
  - create:
      box: music_renderer
      name: window + renderer
      frame: { x: 40.0, y: 40.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          import afield.graphics.vulkan.util.Options
          
          prop<Window>(window)
          prop<Renderer>(renderer)
          
          Options.enableHDR = false
          
          once.renderer {
              window = Window("RectSL — musicality")
              Renderer(window)
          }
          
          println("musicality renderer ready")
          start(renderer::run)
  # 2. groove box — compiles the snippet and draws it live. This is the box you hack on.
  - create:
      box: music_groove
      name: rectsl musicality
      frame: { x: 300.0, y: 140.0, w: 300.0, h: 100.0 }
      properties:
        code: |
          /*
          RectSL's musical layer: the pattern language as scene structure.

          Two facts do all the work. A RectSL track is `sample(t)` and a pattern is
          `events(arc)` — both pure functions of time — so (1) a pattern IS a track,
          which is why `saw ->rotate` needs no conversion word, and (2) a pattern
          event carries an onset and a real duration, which is exactly what
          `->live birth life` wants, so an event IS a life window. `pat` is `array`
          indexed by rhythm instead of by ordinal.

          Nothing below is written in seconds. Edit `rectsl` and re-run to change the
          groove live. See rectsl_cheatsheet.md ("Musicality") / rectsl_examples.md.
          */
          import afield.lang.rectsl.RECT_ANIMATION_VERTEX_SHADER
          import afield.lang.rectsl.RectAnimationOracle
          import afield.lang.rectsl.rectMaterialShaderCode
          import afield.lang.rectsl.writeFrameToMesh

          val rectsl =
              """
          #rectsl
          ->wall 16 9 abstract
          ->tempo 120
          ->beats-per-cycle 4
          ->duration-cycles 4
          ->fps 30
          ->background 0x0a0a12

          # The accent: a full-wall flash, behind everything, on every fourth bar only.
          # This is the thing a loop cannot do and a groove must — `->every` keeps both
          # versions of every track and chooses between them per sample.
          "accent" rect
            16 9 ->wh
            0 0 ->xy
            0xffffff solid ->fill
            0 ->alpha
            ->back
            selected 4 '( 0.14 ->alpha ) ->every
          ;

          # The ring: sixteen slots in space, five of them sounding, the whole figure
          # turning once a bar because `saw` is a pattern read as a rotation track.
          "ring" group
            "hat" rect
              0.26 1.0 ->wh
              0x7cf5d0 solid ->fill
              16 '( f0 tau * ->rot  f0 tau * 3.2 ->polar ) array
              5 16 0 ->euclid
            ;
          end
          "ring" ->select
            saw tau * ->rotate
          ;

          # The kick: one copy per event, each ->live for exactly its own quarter and
          # authored in ITS OWN local time — so sixteen strikes, not a synchronised
          # chorus. `step` places each one across the wall, restarting at every bar line.
          "kick" rect
            1.3 ->square
            0xff5a3c solid ->fill
            "bd*4" '(
                step 1.5 - 4.2 *  ->x
                '( 0=5.5  0.34=0 ) ease-out ->y
                '( 0=0  0.10=1  0.5=0 ) linear ->alpha
            ) pat
          ;

          # The score: the same kind of string, read as a ruler instead of as a rhythm.
          # `pat` spends the subdivision on WHEN, `strip` spends it on WHERE.
          "tick" rect
            0.34 ->square
            0x3c8cff solid ->fill
            "bd [sd sd] hh*4" '( -3.9 ->y  0.55 ->alpha ) strip
          ;
          """

          val program = RectAnimationOracle.compile(rectsl).program!!
          val shader = rectMaterialShaderCode(program)

          /*
          Refresh the generated fragment on every run before `moduleHere {}`; the
          `//%-` fragment break makes this fragment execute first (see the playground
          transcript for the why).
          */
          once.vertex { RECT_ANIMATION_VERTEX_SHADER }
          fragment = shader.exampleFragmentShader!!

          //%-

          val module = moduleHere {
              blend = true
              depthTest = false
              primitiveType = triangles
          }
          val m = Mesh()
          module += "scene" to m
          renderer += "rectsl-musicality" to module

          val ww = program.wall.width.toFloat()
          val wh = program.wall.height.toFloat()
          m.push["worldToClip"] = afield.math.linalg.Matrix4f().ortho(-ww / 2f, ww / 2f, -wh / 2f, wh / 2f, -1f, 1f)
          m.push["wallWidth"] = ww
          m.push["wallHeight"] = wh

          val duration = program.duration.toDouble()
          var t = 0.0
          loop {
              m.push["time"] = t.toFloat()
              program.writeFrameToMesh(t % duration, m)
              t += 1.0 / 60.0
              true
          }
  # 3. wire the groove under the renderer so it inherits Window/Renderer.
  - connect: { parent: music_renderer, child: music_groove }
  # 4. launch the renderer first (it owns the loop), then the groove.
  - launch: { box: music_renderer, property: code, strand: renderer }
  - await: { wait: pending }
  - launch: { box: music_groove, property: code }
  - await: { wait: pending }

              primitiveType = triangles
          }

          module += "scene" to m
          renderer += "rectsl-plot-axes" to module

          val ww = program.wall.width.toFloat()
          val wh = program.wall.height.toFloat()
          m.push["worldToClip"] = afield.math.linalg.Matrix4f().ortho(-ww / 2f, ww / 2f, -wh / 2f, wh / 2f, -1f, 1f)
          m.push["wallWidth"] = ww
          m.push["wallHeight"] = wh

          val duration = program.duration.toDouble()
          var t = 0.0
          loop {
              m.push["time"] = t.toFloat()
              program.writeFrameToMesh(t % duration, m)
              t += 1.0 / 60.0
              true
          }
  # 3. wire the figure under the renderer so it inherits Window/Renderer.
  - connect: { parent: plot_renderer, child: plot_figure }
  # 4. launch the renderer first (it owns the loop), then the figure.
  - launch: { box: plot_renderer, property: code, strand: renderer }
  - await: { wait: pending }
  - launch: { box: plot_figure, property: code }
  - await: { wait: pending }
